subject: Re: MAP — pricing & commitment alignment for Atlas Health
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP and budget constraints — next steps

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to formalize a short Mutual Action Plan so our procurement and security teams can sign off quickly. A few constraints from my side:

- FY27 budget for inference is constrained; target commit is around $300k ARR but we need a stronger unit economics case.
- Our procurement team will prioritize any proposal that includes either an onboarding credit or a short-term usage credit to offset migration costs.
- Timeline: procurement aims to get to PO within 3 weeks of a formal pricing agreement.

High-level ask from Atlas: 30% discount on list pricing + $50k onboarding credit if we commit to ~$300k ARR within 12 months. If you have tiered commit/discounts, please share so we can weigh internally. Also can you share a MAP spreadsheet (milestones, owners, dates) that we can circulate to our ops and procurement leads?

I can join a MAP checkpoint meeting if helpful — mornings PT are best for me.

Thanks,
Maria Garcia
Director, Clinical Data Integrations
Atlas Health

Attachments: initial_budget_constraints.pdf (see procurement notes)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP and budget constraints — next steps

Maria — thanks for the clear context. We can absolutely put a MAP together and propose a couple of structured pricing options so procurement can evaluate them quickly. Proposed next steps:

1) MAP doc & pricing options (attached): I attached MAP_v2_atlas_health.xlsx and pricing_model_v3.pdf — please review and we'll iterate.
2) Internal approvals required on our side: sales ops (Neha) for discount guidance and legal (Dev) for any deviation from standard terms. I’ve looped them in the internal thread.
3) Suggested tiered commit (initial proposal to start discussion):
   - Commit $250k ARR -> 15% discount, no onboarding credit
   - Commit $300k ARR -> 20% discount + $30k onboarding credit
   - Commit $500k ARR -> 25% discount + $50k onboarding credit + extended SLOs

We’re open to discussion; the pricing_model_v3 has more granular unit economics and an example run-rate calculation tied to your expected monthly throughput. If you and procurement are aligned on a target commit, we can put a recommended addendum together for DocuSign review.

Can we schedule a 30-minute MAP checkpoint on Monday 7/6 9:30am PT? If that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite and a short meeting agenda.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_v2_atlas_health.xlsx; pricing_model_v3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP and budget constraints — next steps

Looping in a couple technical clarifications from my side so the MAP includes acceptance criteria for your evaluation:

- Pilot dataset scope: confirm the three sample pipelines (EHR export, normalizer, embeddings) and estimated peak concurrent tokens.
- Latency SLOs: we'll propose a 99th-percentile target consistent with dedicated deployments for the pilot.
- Security: Maria, procurement may ask for a concise SOC2 summary. I’ve pulled our short SOC2_summary.pdf and will attach it to the MAP folder in Drive.

I’ll prepare short test cases that map to the MAP milestones so your engineering and procurement teams can see objective criteria for go/no-go decisions.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Atlas — pricing recommendation and approval path

Internal — quick note from sales ops/finance after I reviewed the MAP and the suggested tiers. High level recommendation and gating items:

- Recommended counter to Atlas (what we will present at MAP checkpoint):
   - Offer: Commit $300k ARR -> 20% discount + $30k onboarding credit (de-escalates their 30% ask while preserving margin).
   - If Atlas commits to $500k ARR, escalate to Director approval for 25% + $50k credit and standard enterprise SLOs.

- Approvals required: VP Sales approval for any discount >20% or credits >$30k. Legal (Dev) will need to review an addendum for any non-standard credit language.
- Timing: I can get a VP approval by EOD Thu 7/8 if we lock a written request today; legal turnaround for a short addendum ~48 hours once we have the final language.

Action items for internal owners:
- Karthik: get explicit procurement target (PO date and contact) from Atlas during the MAP checkpoint.
- Marissa: confirm pilot acceptance criteria and share test-case doc to Drive by 7/7.
- Dev: standby to review addendum once I confirm final credit/discount numbers.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sales Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: MAP alignment — agreed next steps, owners, and timeline (summary)

Maria — thanks for the MAP checkpoint earlier this morning. Quick summary and agreed points so procurement and your ops team have a single source of truth:

1) Pricing & commit (agreed for procurement review):
   - Atlas target: $300k ARR commit
   - Redwood proposal: 20% discount + $30k onboarding credit (sales ops approved at >15% via Neha; Neha will route VP approval if anything changes)

2) Timeline & PO expectations:
   - Atlas procurement target: PO issued by 7/29/2026 (Maria to confirm internal PO owner and exact date).
   - Redwood will prepare a pricing addendum and DocuSign packet once Atlas confirms final commit; expected legal turnaround ~48 hours after submission.

3) Technical & evaluation plan (milestones):
   - Pilot start: 7/15/2026 (engineering handoff) — Marissa to deliver acceptance test cases by 7/7.
   - Pilot completion and eval: 8/14/2026 — objective metrics in MAP spreadsheet.

4) Action items (owners):
   - Maria (Atlas): confirm PO owner and procurement target date (by 7/9).
   - Karthik (Redwood): prepare pricing addendum draft and DocuSign (by 7/9).
   - Neha (Redwood): route for VP approval if final ask exceeds current recommendation.
   - Marissa (Redwood): upload acceptance tests to Drive and confirm pilot runbook (by 7/7).
   - Dev (Redwood): review addendum once drafted.

Attachments uploaded to shared Drive: MAP_v2_atlas_health.xlsx, pricing_model_v3.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345
Drive MAP folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/atlas-map

If I don’t hear objections from your procurement team by EOD Friday (7/9), we’ll prepare the addendum and route DocuSign. Appreciate the partnership — we’ll aim to keep the MAP tight and remove blockers quickly.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
